verified.resolved_title: Exploring programmatic moderators of the effectiveness of marriage and relationship education programs: a meta-analytic study.
verified.note: The DOI in the record (10.1016/j.beth.2011.03.006) resolves via esearch to PMID 22304884 = Sher TG, 'What, why, and for whom: couples interventions: a deconstruction approach' (Behav Ther 2012;43(1):123-31) -- a commentary, NOT the 148-report moderators meta-analysis. That is a wrong/hallucinated DOI. The actual paper matching the claim (148 evaluation reports; 9-20 contact-hour moderate-dosage programs stronger than 1-8 h low-dosage; communication-focused emphasis -> stronger communication-outcome effects but not significant for relationship quality/satisfaction) is Hawkins AJ, Stanley SM, Blanchard VL, Albright M (2012), same journal/issue, DOI 10.1016/j.beth.2010.12.006, PMID 22304880. EXACT CORRECTION: id should be PMID 22304880 (or DOI 10.1016/j.beth.2010.12.006), first author Hawkins AJ (with Stanley SM, Blanchard VL, Albright M), year 2012 -- not 'Hawkins/Blanchard?' as a guess and not the currently-cited DOI. Also resolves the claim's own '(Behavior Therapy 2012?)' uncertainty flag: confirmed Behav Ther 2012;43(1):77-87.

verified.resolved_title: Comparing the effects of premarital booklet- and video-based educations on the reproductive health literacy of engaged couples.
verified.note: Abstract confirms 110 couples (55 BBE + 55 VBE), and significant time-group interaction for access to information, evaluation of information, and decision-making/application dimensions, matching the claim closely. MINOR FIX: the study is described in the abstract as a 'quasi-experimental study' with couples 'purposefully recruited and randomly allocated' -- calling it simply a '2024 trial' overstates rigor slightly (not an RCT with random sampling from a defined population); more precise wording is 'quasi-experimental comparison'. Also note the reading-and-understanding RHL dimension showed NO significant time-group interaction (p=0.56) -- the claim's 'incl. access, evaluation, decision-making/application' is accurate as far as it goes but should not be extended to imply all RHL dimensions improved equally.
